content_sections.text: The fellow will work on the project "Development of a Functionally Graded Weld Joints Between Ferritic/Martensitic P91 to Austenitic SS 304 Steel through TIG Welding for High Temperature Applications" under the mentorship of Prof. D K Dwivedi. content_sections.heading: IIT Roorkee Post Doctoral Fellow Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: You must have a Ph.D. in Mechanical / Manufacturing or allied Metallurgical Engineering. You also need a research background in metal processing and joining, with a good publication record. These are preferred but not required: Prior experience in dissimilar metal welding Strong expertise in material characterization Expertise in numerical modeling skills and finite element simulation of manufacturing processes Research experience in development of functionally graded materials The official notification has the full eligibility details for this post.

content_sections.heading: Important Dates
content_sections.text: The notice says applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Applications will be screened, and the screened candidates will be called for interview.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: The fellowship lasts 2 years. Either side can end the fellowship by giving one month's notice. The position is purely temporary. Post-doctoral Fellows are registered as students and may use the library, computer center, available hospital facilities and other facilities. Fellows get 2.5 days of leave for each completed calendar month. Leave cannot be carried forward beyond the calendar year.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for IIT Roorkee Post Doctoral Fellow Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Open the IIT Roorkee PDF online application form . The notice says applications are accepted only through this online form. Fill in the form and submit it before 11.59 PM on 12 November 2026. If you are shortlisted after screening, you will be called for an interview.

faq.question: Q1. Which project will the Post Doctoral Fellow work on?
faq.answer: The project is "Development of a Functionally Graded Weld Joints Between Ferritic/Martensitic P91 to Austenitic SS 304 Steel through TIG Welding for High Temperature Applications". The mentor is Prof. D K Dwivedi.

faq.question: Q2. Which Ph.D. subjects can apply?
faq.answer: A Ph.D. in Mechanical / Manufacturing or allied Metallurgical Engineering. You also need a research background in metal processing and joining and a good publication record.

faq.question: Q3. Is there any grant besides the monthly fellowship?
faq.answer: Yes. Post-Doctoral Fellows also get a contingency grant of Rs. 50,000.00 per annum.

faq.question: Q4. Can the fellowship end before two years?
faq.answer: Yes. Either side can end it by giving one month's notice.

faq.question: Q5. How much leave does a Post Doctoral Fellow get?
faq.answer: 2.5 days for each completed calendar month. Unused leave cannot be carried forward beyond the calendar year.

faq.question: Q6. What facilities do fellows get on campus?
faq.answer: Fellows are registered as students. They may use the library, the computer center, available hospital facilities and other facilities.

faq.question: Q7. Is this a permanent position?
faq.answer: No. The notice says PDF positions are purely temporary.

faq.question: Q8. Will there be an interview?
faq.answer: Yes. Candidates who clear the screening will be called for an interview.

faq.question: Q9. What experience gives an applicant an advantage?
faq.answer: The notice prefers experience in dissimilar metal welding, material characterization, numerical modeling and finite element simulation, and research on functionally graded materials.
